title: Hall-type criterion for a perfect matching in a bipartite graph
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ that is bipartite with parts $X$ and $Y$: the sets $X$ and $Y$ are disjoint, together they exhaust $V$ (so $X \cup Y = V$), and every edge of $G$ joins a vertex of $X$ to a vertex of $Y$. For a set $S \subseteq V$ write $N(S) = \bigcup_{v \in S} N(v)$ for the set of all vertices adjacent to some vertex of $S$. Then $G$ has a perfect matching if and only if $\abs{S} \le \abs{N(S)}$ for every set $S \subseteq V$.
hypotheses_covered: G is bipartite with parts X and Y
X and Y cover all vertices (X ∪ Y = V)
